questions.question: What does NVIDIA say drove its revenue growth in fiscal year 2026, and what external constraints and product-transition challenges does it highlight in its FY2026 MD&A?

answer.text:
NVIDIA reported fiscal year 2026 revenue of $215.9 billion, up 65% from $130.5 billion a year earlier [0001045810-26-000021:0063]. It says Data Center revenue rose 68%, driven by the major platform shifts of accelerated computing and AI [0001045810-26-000021:0063]. Gaming revenue rose 41% on strong Blackwell demand [0001045810-26-000021:0063]. Professional Visualization rose 70%, driven by exceptional Blackwell demand and the launch of DGX Spark [0001045810-26-000021:0063]. Automotive rose 39% on continued adoption of its self-driving platforms [0001045810-26-000021:0063].
The one external constraint the FY2026 MD&A excerpt names is supply: NVIDIA expects supply constraints to be a headwind to Gaming in the first quarter of fiscal 2027 and beyond [0001045810-26-000021:0063]. They also say reduced demand from export controls could lead to excess inventory or related supply charges [0001045810-26-000021:0041]. The same section says China's antitrust regulators published a preliminary finding on September 15, 2025 that NVIDIA's compliance with U.S. export controls violated the terms of China's approval of its Mellanox acquisition [0001045810-26-000021:0041]. The Q1 FY2026 10-Q adds that H20 export licensing requirements affected current revenue and will negatively affect future revenue [0001045810-25-000116:0031].
On product transition, gross margin fell to 71.1% from 75.0%, a decline of 3.9 points, as the business model moved from Hopper HGX systems to Blackwell full-scale datacenter solutions [0001045810-26-000021:0063]. The decline was also affected by a $4.5 billion charge for H20 excess inventory and purchase obligations [0001045810-26-000021:0063]. Operating expenses rose 41% to $23,076 million, driven by higher compensation and benefits from employee growth and by compute and infrastructure costs [0001045810-26-000021:0063].

questions.question: How was Intel's sale of a majority stake in Altera structured, and how did it affect Intel's FY2025 financial statements?

answer.text:
Intel signed a transaction agreement on April 14, 2025 to sell 51% of the issued and outstanding common stock of Altera, then a wholly owned subsidiary, to SLP VII Gryphon Aggregator, L.P., an affiliate of SLP [0000050863-26-000011:0145]. The sale closed on September 12, 2025 for net purchase consideration of $4.3 billion [0000050863-26-000011:0145]. That consideration consisted of $4.3 billion in cash received at closing, $500 million in deferred cash proceeds received in the third quarter of 2025, and $500 million in deferred cash proceeds payable no later than December 31, 2027 [0000050863-26-000011:0145]. It was offset by $400 million of cash transferred to Altera, about $469 million of separation and employee-related costs Intel agreed to fund to SLP, and other direct and incremental costs of the sale [0000050863-26-000011:0145].
Altera was deconsolidated effective September 12, 2025, and its results were included in Intel's "all other" category through September 11, 2025 [0000050863-26-000011:0039]. Intel's retained interest is accounted for under the equity method and classified within equity investments [0000050863-26-000011:0145]. At December 27, 2025 its carrying value was $3.2 billion and Intel's ownership interest was 48% [0000050863-26-000011:0145].
The sale produced a $5.6 billion pre-tax gain, recognized in interest and other, net [0000050863-26-000011:0046]. This was partly offset in that line by a $1.8 billion net loss from the change in fair value of the derivative liability for the Escrowed Shares and by $229 million of charges related to the sale of the NAND memory business [0000050863-26-000011:0046]. The 2025 effective tax rate was 98.3%, and the filing says the nonrecurring Altera gain partly offset the effect of the valuation allowance change on that rate [0000050863-26-000011:0046].
On the balance sheet at December 27, 2025, Intel had a $463 million receivable from SLP in other long-term assets for the present value of the deferred consideration [0000050863-26-000011:0145]. It also had $327 million in other accrued liabilities and $97 million in other long-term liabilities for unpaid separation and employee-related costs owed to SLP [0000050863-26-000011:0145]. Intel is still finalizing customary closing adjustments, which may change the final net cash proceeds and the gain on sale [0000050863-26-000011:0145].
"All other" revenue was $3.6 billion in 2025, down $38 million from 2024, mainly because of lower revenue from other non-reportable segments after the Altera divestiture, largely offset by higher Mobileye revenue [0000050863-26-000011:0039]. "All other" operating income was $264 million in 2025, compared with an operating loss of $57 million in 2024, helped by improved Altera operating income contribution [0000050863-26-000011:0039].
Intel also provides wafer manufacturing services to Altera, now a related party, and expects reimbursement for corporate services under a transition services agreement [0000050863-26-000011:0145].

questions.question: What did Intel's 2024 Restructuring Plan involve, and when did Intel expect it to be substantially completed, per the FY2024 10-K?

answer.text:
Intel's 2024 Restructuring Plan was a set of cost and capital reduction initiatives meant to adjust spending to current business trends while enabling its new operating model and continuing to fund investments in its core strategy of returning to product and process competitiveness [0000050863-25-000009:0021]. The initiatives include reducing headcount, consolidating and reducing the global real estate footprint, conducting portfolio reviews of its businesses under a "clean sheet" view, rationalizing capital investments and deployments based on demand signals and capacity requirements, and reducing overall operating expenses [0000050863-25-000009:0021]. The headcount actions were expected to result in an approximate 15% decrease in Intel's core workforce by early 2025 [0000050863-25-000009:0021][0000050863-25-000009:0016].
The plan was announced in Q3 2024, then approved and committed to by management, to implement cost-reduction measures including reductions in employee headcount, other operating expenditures, and capital expenditures [0000050863-25-000009:0039]. Its charges are primarily employee severance and benefit arrangements, non-cash asset impairments tied to exit activities, and charges for real estate exits and consolidations [0000050863-25-000009:0123]. Intel recognized restructuring charges of $2.8 billion in 2024 and expects total charges of approximately $3.0 billion under the plan [0000050863-25-000009:0021][0000050863-25-000009:0123].
Intel expected actions under the plan to be substantially completed by the fourth quarter of 2025, which is subject to change [0000050863-25-000009:0039][0000050863-25-000009:0123].

questions.question: What did Intel's FY2024 10-K say about its policy on dividends and stock repurchases, and what constrains its ability to return cash to stockholders?

answer.text:
Intel said it has ceased to return capital to stockholders: in recent years it has not made stock repurchases, and it reduced and then suspended its quarterly dividend in the fourth quarter of 2024 [0000050863-25-000009:0073]. Its last share repurchase under its authorization occurred in Q1 2021, and no shares were repurchased during the fiscal year ended December 28, 2024 [0000050863-25-000009:0083][0000050863-25-000009:0084]. As of December 28, 2024, Intel was authorized to repurchase up to $110.0 billion, of which $7.2 billion remained available [0000050863-25-000009:0083][0000050863-25-000009:0084]. Intel is not obligated to make repurchases under the program, and it gave no assurance about the amount, timing or execution of future repurchases or that any repurchases would enhance long-term stockholder value [0000050863-25-000009:0073]. Shares withheld for tax purposes on RSU vesting are treated as common stock repurchases in the Consolidated Financial Statements but are not counted as repurchases under the authorized program [0000050863-25-000009:0084].
The filing names one explicit constraint on dividends: under its commercial CHIPS Act agreement, Intel agreed to forgo paying dividends for the next two years and to limits on dividend payments for the three years after that [0000050863-25-000009:0073]. Intel also said there can be no assurance that it will be able to pay dividends in the future [0000050863-25-000009:0073].
It had $51.0 billion in aggregate principal amount of senior unsecured notes and other borrowings outstanding as of December 28, 2024, and it said its debt level and debt service obligations could reduce its flexibility [0000050863-25-000009:0073]. It also reported a net loss attributable to Intel of $18,756 million for FY2024 [0000050863-25-000009:0092]. Its funding requirements include capital expenditures, with commitments of $14.0 billion for 2025 and $6.0 billion in the long term [0000050863-25-000009:0042].

Intel's products business would, over time, depend on third-party foundries, particularly TSMC, as it develops products for nodes beyond Intel 18A and Intel 18A-P [0000050863-26-000011:0065]. If it could not secure and maintain enough capacity on favorable pricing terms, it might be unable to make its products in sufficient volume and at a cost that supports its products business [0000050863-26-000011:0065]. Most of its competitors have longer and more established relationships with TSMC and other third-party foundries, which could put Intel at a competitive disadvantage [0000050863-26-000011:0065]. Only TSMC and Samsung can currently produce the leading-edge and near-leading-edge nodes Intel's products need [0000050863-26-000011:0065]. If competitors were more successful in securing capacity with those foundries, Intel's product roadmap, market position and customer relationships would be materially adversely impacted [0000050863-26-000011:0065].

questions.question: What is the status of the third Texas patent case and the related license defense in Intel's VLSI litigation, according to the FY2025 10-K?

answer.text:
The third Texas case went to trial in November 2022 with VLSI asserting one remaining patent, and the jury found the patent valid and infringed and awarded VLSI approximately $949 million in damages, plus interest and a running royalty [0000050863-26-000011:0176]. The court has not yet entered final judgment [0000050863-26-000011:0176]. In February 2023, Intel filed motions for a new trial and for judgment as a matter of law notwithstanding the verdict, and further appeals are possible [0000050863-26-000011:0176].
On the license defense, Intel moved in April 2024 to add the defense that it is licensed to VLSI's patents, and the court granted the motion that same month [0000050863-26-000011:0176]. In May 2025, the court held a trial on an underlying factual question relating to the license defense, and the jury returned a verdict in Intel's favor [0000050863-26-000011:0176]. Post-trial briefing is complete, and the court will address the ultimate legal issue of whether Intel obtained a license to the asserted VLSI patent through its license agreement with Finjan when Fortress Investments acquired Finjan [0000050863-26-000011:0176].
The Delaware court has not taken further action and continues to receive status reports from the parties regarding the Texas court's consideration of Intel's license defense [0000050863-26-000011:0176].
As of December 27, 2025, Intel had accrued a charge of approximately $1.0 billion related to the VLSI litigation and was unable to make a reasonable estimate of losses in excess of recorded amounts [0000050863-26-000011:0177].
